What changed and how to read this comparison

The first language batch added 94 encoded letters for Polish, Czech, Hungarian, Romanian, Turkish, Hausa, Kurdish (Kurmanji, Latin), Māori, Igbo, and Uzbek (Latin). Their pinned CLDR main, auxiliary, and index alphabets, both cases, and canonical forms are audited in every style and Latin extended subset. Turkish retains the dot in fi words; Romanian legacy cedillas use comma forms under lang="ro". Hungarian uppercase digraphs get extra clearance under lang="hu". The language selector sets the actual text language.

Phase 4 preserves every licensed 0.36 outline, advance, approved pair value and design setting. The 0.35 stroke-join repair carries forward. The foundation, numeric features, joins, and cursor stops carry forward. Phase 4 adds complete Latin Extended-A, common Slavic Cyrillic, monotonic Greek and full Vietnamese. Baseline 0.34 and the reference fonts can use browser fallback for unsupported characters; those rows are not evidence of encoded coverage. Alphabet and shaping coverage is separate from native-reader or device certification. Vietnamese includes all encoded tones and horn vowels; polytonic Greek and other scripts remain outside this batch.

Compare 20px at 1.4 and 1.5 line height, then 13/15/17px at Regular and Medium. Use Full reading width for longer lines. The sample can help identify differences; sustained reading and the readability guidance still call for feedback from readers.

Material's body-text guidance suggests around 1.5 line height. Google's web-font guide covers weight/style mapping and font loading. This page embeds the real fonts and makes no network font requests.

References: Literata 3.103 and Rubik 2.300, under the SIL Open Font License. Licenses and source hashes are kept in references/. SEIReader is an original SEIHouse design.
